To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the surface modification of cellulose nanocrystals with PMMA significantly improves the mechanical and biodegradable properties of a 75:25 LDPE/TPSthermoplastic starch composite.
the addition of CNF and PMMA-grafted CNFs into a 75/ 25 LDPE/TPSthermoplastic starch blend improved the tensile strength, Young’s modulus, elongation at break and water absorption of the composites.
the addition of cellulose nanomaterials to LDPE/TPSthermoplastic starch blend can improve its mechanical properties and biodegradability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to improve mechanical properties and biodegradability of LDPE/TPSthermoplastic composites.
the preparation of LDPE/TPSthermo-plastic starch composites reinforced with CNFs and CNF-g-poly (MMA) and the investigation of the mechanical properties and degradable behavior of the composites.
the preparation of LDPE/TPSB blend nanocomposites using cellulose nanofibrils and PMMA-grafted cellulose nanocomposite.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the surface modification of CNFs by PMMA grafting has a significant impact on mechanical properties and degradation rate of the LDPE-based nanocomposites.
the addition of PMMA-grafted cellulose nanocomposite to LDPE/TPSB improved the mechanical properties of the composite and also enhanced its degradability.
the addition of cellulose nanocrystals to LDPE/TPSto improve mechanical properties is a viable approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cellulose nanofiber can be used as a reinforcing material in the LDPE/thermoset polymer blends.
the mechanical and biodegradable properties of LDPE/TPs blend could be improved by using cellulose nanofiber.
the addition of PMMA-grafted cellulose nanocomposite to a LDPE/thermo plastic starch blend can improve the mechanical properties and biodegradability of the blend.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the addition of PMMA-grafted cellulose nanowhiskers to LDPE/TP blend can be used to improve the mechanical properties and biodegradability of LDPE/TP blends, and this can be used in the development of biodegradable materials.
cellulose nanofibrils can be used as reinforcing agents in LDPE/TPSto enhance their mechanical properties and to improve their biodegradability.
cellulose nanofiber grafting with PMMA can be used to improve the mechanical properties of LDPE/TPSthermoplastic starch blends.
